Iran International live blog, 24 October 2026

The US military has prepared options for renewed strikes on Iran after November’s midterm elections, The Hill reported Saturday, citing two sources familiar with the planning. One source said US Central Command had follow-up strike plans ready pending White House authorization.

President Donald Trump said the United States could strike Iran as soon as “tomorrow” or reach an agreement with the Islamic Republic, adding he wanted a permanent solution to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon.

US warships are preparing for possible strikes against Iran, with sailors loading munitions and readying aircraft aboard the USS George Washington aircraft carrier strike group, The Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday.

The US is moving some diplomats and families out of Lebanon, the UAE, Qatar and Jordan, CNN reported. Axios said intelligence on alleged Iranian assassination plots helped prompt the staffing reductions.

The Saudi-led coalition said on Sunday it intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile fired by the Houthis toward Khamis Mushait.

Iran’s army said on Sunday that its air defense systems shot down a US LUCAS drone over the southern port city of Bandar Abbas.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that US bases have become the main source of insecurity for their host countries, and the region should move toward having no foreign troops.

“The decisive action of our armed forces shattered all foreign security calculations,” Araghchi said. He added that Iran’s regional policy remained based on security built within the region and without foreign interference.

Araghchi called recent developments, particularly the 40-day war, a turning point that had changed the region’s previous security structures.

He said Iran’s policies would not change whether or not fighting resumed, adding that he was already thinking about the postwar period.

“They tried war twice and got no result. If they try it once more, they will get no different result,” Araghchi said. “If they have any sense, they will not try aggression again.”

100%Oct 25, 2026, 06:56 GMT+0Iranian lawmaker says parliament will question minister over internet price hikeIran’s parliament plans to question the communications minister about a 40% increase in internet tariffs, a lawmaker said on Sunday, adding that the price rise had gone ahead without promised improvements to service quality or reduced filtering.

Mostafa Pourdeghan, a member of parliament’s industries and mines committee, told ILNA that lawmakers had supported higher tariffs only if operators improved internet quality and filtering was eased.

“The price increase happened, but the conditions set by the committee and the commitments made were not fulfilled,” he said.

The Gabd-Rimdan border crossing between Iran and Pakistan has reopened, allowing trucks carrying liquefied gas and essential goods to resume transit, the IRGC-linked Fars news agency reported on Sunday.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s visit to Tehran during a period of repeated US and Israeli threats showed that Iran-Russia relations were too deep to be overshadowed by other issues, Iranian lawmaker Ebrahim Rezaei said on Sunday.

An Iranian lawmaker said on Sunday that any country that allows the United States to use its territory or airspace to attack Iran would become a “legitimate military target.”

“Today, the Islamic Republic has set aside restraint to show everyone that it will not compromise on its national interests,” Ruhollah Mousavi Bideli said.

He warned regional countries against helping the US and said regional security required the withdrawal of the United States and Israel from the Persian Gulf, followed by regional states taking responsibility for their own security.

100%Oct 25, 2026, 05:49 GMT+0Iran lawmaker says agencies have been slow to compensate war damageThe performance of the Iranian government agencies in delivering on promises to compensate for damage and address war-related issues has been weak, parliament’s planning, budget and accounts committee chairman Gholamreza Tajgardoun said on Sunday.

The Israeli military began a preplanned exercise simulating a multifront attack on Sunday.

The drill will run through Monday in northern and central Israel, involving the air force and the military’s Northern and Central commands.

The IDF said troops would practice scenarios including a surprise attack and an air and ground infiltration. It said there was no concern about a real security incident.

Baghdad’s pledge to stay out of renewed fighting is being tested by reported Israeli jet flights toward Iran through Iraqi airspace, suspected strikes on militia stores reportedly holding Chinese-made air defenses, and drone attacks on Iranian Kurdish opposition bases.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi says Iraq will not participate in any war, while Iran-backed factions describe supporting Tehran against the United States and Israel as a duty, raising questions over Baghdad’s ability to control how its territory and airspace are used.

“Iraq will not participate in any war,” Zaidi told state-run Al-Iraqiya television on Friday, saying Baghdad wanted to remain a meeting point for regional rivals and was working to ease the confrontation between Iran and the United States.
